source: Written for english/y7 lesson 52 (Biography 'Refaat Alareer: A Teacher of Stories' (teacher-written from published facts only, pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 52. A short biography written for TGA from published facts only. Read it, then answer the questions and complete the comparison with the poem.

passage.title: Refaat Alareer: A Teacher of Stories
paras: Refaat Alareer was born in Gaza in 1979. He grew up loving stories, and he became a teacher of English literature at the Islamic University of Gaza, where he taught for many years. His students remember him as a patient, demanding teacher who believed that stories matter: that telling your own story is a way of being seen.

Alareer did not only write; he helped others to write. In 2014 he edited Gaza Writes Back, a collection of short stories by young writers from Gaza. He also helped to start We Are Not Numbers, a project in which young Palestinian writers are paired with mentors so that they can tell their own stories in English, as people rather than statistics.

He wrote poems too. In 2011 he first shared a short poem called 'If I Must Die', in which the speaker asks that, if he dies, his story be told and that it 'bring hope'. Alareer was killed in December 2023, during the war in Gaza. In the weeks that followed, his poem was shared and read aloud around the world and translated into many languages.
A biography cannot tell everything about a life. This one chooses to tell of a teacher, a mentor and a writer, and of the young writers who carry his work on.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'Compare how the biography and the poem present Alareer's legacy.' Starter: 'Both texts suggest that his legacy is...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph: biography shows legacy through his students and books; the poem through the kite and the plea to 'tell my story'.

questions.q: Extend: write one sentence on why biographers must not invent details
questions.a: A biography claims to be true, so invented details would mislead readers and wrong the person.

questions.q: Stretch: what makes a good mentor? Use the biography and your own experience
questions.a: Patience, belief in others, practical help: he helped young people write and publish.

questions.q: How does knowing he was a teacher of stories change our reading of 'tell my story'?
options: it shows his legacy is passing stories on, as he taught others to
it shows he did not like teaching
it makes no difference at all
questions.a: A) it shows his legacy is passing stories on, as he taught others to. He spent his life helping others tell stories; the poem asks us to do the same for him.

questions.q: Gaza Writes Back (2014) contains stories by...
Answer the ponder: does the poet's life change how you read the poem?
questions.a: For example: yes; 'tell my story' sounds like a teacher's last lesson.
